product_scope.problem_statement: The current workflow implementation carries redundant branches, inconsistent persistence shapes, and runtime type mismatches that break successful and failure closures after a work item has already been claimed.
product_scope.goal: Replace the current workflow with a new clean state machine that keeps the same business intent but uses a simpler and safer execution model for idempotency, pending lifecycle, consumer invocation, retries, and final closure.
success_outcomes: A successful work item reaches a single stable success closure path without leaving IN_PROGRESS records behind.
A terminal provider failure reaches a single stable failure closure path without retry.
A transient provider failure retries and then closes through one stable exhausted-failure path if attempts are consumed.
An unexpected internal failure closes through an explicit unexpected path instead of being disguised as a provider transient failure.
The workflow writes operational evidence with one consistent result shape across success and failure.
The workflow remains simple enough to reason about state by state during manual AWS debugging.

in_scope: Rebuild of the Step Functions Express workflow for the current phase-3 runtime.
Simplification of success, terminal, transient exhausted, timeout, and unexpected closure paths.
Idempotency claim and duplicate handling semantics.
Pending record lifecycle transitions from PENDING to IN_PROGRESS to COMPLETED or FAILED.
Final persistence behavior in tapi-results, tapi-idempotency, and tapi-pending-records.
Manual debuggability through stable state transitions and deterministic input contracts.
out_of_scope: Changes to the producer slot-query model.
Changes to SQS FIFO provider isolation semantics.
Changes to the scheduler topology of 288 slots.
Replay tooling, dashboards, or operator UI.
Changes to the external provider API contract beyond the existing classified consumer behavior.

actors.name: EventBridge Pipe
actors.description: Starts one workflow execution per FIFO work item and passes the canonical work item payload.

actors.name: State Machine
actors.description: Owns operational lifecycle, retry policy, state transitions, and final closure.

actors.name: Consumer Lambda
actors.description: Executes the provider API call and returns or throws business outcomes.

actors.name: Operator
actors.description: Debugs failures directly in AWS using workflow input, logs, and DynamoDB state.

user_journeys.name: Successful work item closes cleanly
steps: A new work item starts execution from the FIFO queue.
The workflow claims idempotency and moves the pending record to IN_PROGRESS.
The workflow persists success evidence and closes idempotency and pending state as completed.

user_journeys.name: Terminal provider failure closes immediately
steps: The consumer reports a terminal provider failure.
The workflow skips retry and routes directly to failure closure.
The workflow persists failure evidence and marks the work item as failed.

user_journeys.name: Transient provider failure exhausts retries and closes
steps: The consumer reports a retryable provider failure.
The workflow retries according to the configured backoff behavior.
If retries are exhausted, the workflow persists exhausted failure evidence and marks the work item as failed.

user_journeys.name: Unexpected internal failure is visible as unexpected
steps: An internal or workflow-level error occurs that is not a classified provider failure.
The workflow closes through an explicit unexpected path.
The final evidence clearly distinguishes the failure from provider terminal or transient outcomes.

user_journeys.name: Duplicate or stale-claimable work item ends safely
steps: A duplicate or no-longer-claimable work item starts execution.
The workflow cannot safely claim the logical work item or pending record.
The workflow ends without making a second provider call.

use_cases.title: Claim one logical work item before business execution
use_cases.description: The workflow must prevent duplicate provider execution for the same logical work item.

use_cases.title: Advance and close lifecycle state consistently
use_cases.description: The workflow must reflect operational progress in both pending and idempotency records.

use_cases.title: Differentiate classified provider failures from unexpected failures
use_cases.description: The workflow must preserve the semantic difference between terminal, transient, timeout, and unexpected outcomes.

use_cases.title: Persist one consistent result contract
use_cases.description: The workflow must write success and failure evidence in a shape that can be read uniformly.

use_cases.title: Support direct AWS console debugging
use_cases.description: The workflow must remain easy to test manually with one input payload and predictable state transitions.

business_rules.rule: The workflow remains the single owner of operational closure and final persistence.
The consumer Lambda remains responsible only for provider execution and classified business outcomes.
A work item must be claimed before any provider call is attempted.
A duplicate or non-claimable work item must not trigger a second provider execution.
Terminal failures must not be retried.
Only transient failures may consume the retry policy.
Unexpected internal failures must remain distinguishable from provider failures.
The final results contract must stay consistent enough to be queried and audited without branch-specific parsing rules.
The workflow must avoid leaving pending and idempotency state indefinitely in IN_PROGRESS after a closure attempt.

functional_requirements.title: Canonical workflow input
functional_requirements.statement: The new workflow must accept one canonical work item input that can be executed directly from AWS for debugging.

functional_requirements.title: Single idempotency claim behavior
functional_requirements.statement: The workflow must attempt exactly one logical claim before business execution and end safely when the claim cannot be made.

functional_requirements.title: Single in-progress transition behavior
functional_requirements.statement: The workflow must transition an eligible pending record into IN_PROGRESS before invoking the consumer.

functional_requirements.title: Explicit success closure
functional_requirements.statement: The workflow must close successful executions through one success path that persists final evidence and marks the work item completed.

functional_requirements.title: Explicit terminal closure
functional_requirements.statement: The workflow must close terminal failures through one direct failure path without retry.

functional_requirements.title: Explicit transient exhausted closure
functional_requirements.statement: The workflow must close exhausted retry outcomes through one final transient failure path.

functional_requirements.title: Explicit unexpected closure
functional_requirements.statement: The workflow must close unexpected internal failures through a dedicated unexpected path.

functional_requirements.title: Consistent persistence contract
functional_requirements.statement: The workflow must write final result evidence in a uniform shape across success and failure outcomes.

functional_requirements.title: No silent stuck closure
functional_requirements.statement: The workflow must be designed so that a closure-path failure does not silently look like a completed business execution while leaving lifecycle rows stuck in IN_PROGRESS.

acceptance_criteria.given: A valid pending work item starts execution
acceptance_criteria.when: The workflow runs end to end successfully
acceptance_criteria.then: It must invoke the consumer once, persist success evidence, mark idempotency completed, and mark the pending record completed.

acceptance_criteria.given: The consumer reports a terminal failure
acceptance_criteria.then: It must skip retry, persist terminal failure evidence, and close the work item as failed.

acceptance_criteria.given: The consumer reports a transient failure repeatedly
acceptance_criteria.then: The workflow must persist exhausted transient failure evidence and close the work item as failed.
The final evidence must identify the outcome as unexpected rather than terminal or transient provider failure.

acceptance_criteria.given: A duplicate or non-claimable work item starts execution
acceptance_criteria.when: The workflow cannot safely claim it
acceptance_criteria.then: It must end without invoking the consumer a second time.

acceptance_criteria.given: An operator manually tests the workflow from the AWS console
acceptance_criteria.when: They use a real DynamoDB-backed work item payload
acceptance_criteria.then: They must be able to tell from the state machine where the execution failed and why.

acceptance_criteria.given: A reviewer compares success and failure results
acceptance_criteria.then: They must not need branch-specific type assumptions to understand the stored outcome.

assumptions: The workflow remains an Express state machine triggered synchronously by EventBridge Pipe.
The current consumer classification contract remains the source of transient versus terminal provider outcomes.
Duplicate work items may continue to close as no-op completions rather than explicit business failures, unless the technical design proves that stale-lock recovery must be modeled differently.
The rebuild may remove or collapse existing intermediate parsing and normalization states if the same functional behavior is preserved more safely.

open_questions.question: Should duplicate-claim detection remain a silent no-op completion, or should stale IN_PROGRESS evidence be surfaced differently if the new technical design can distinguish it safely?
